subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352; PB353. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR20): 'If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to 1 if records exist in the physical file. If no records exist in the file, or the physical file does not support the ability to position at the first record, the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to 23, the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' The construct is unambiguously legal: 14.9.41.3 SR2 (cite.py --check OK) says 'If the organization of the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequential, either the FIRST or the LAST phrase shall be specified'; 9.1.8.2 (cite.py --check OK) says 'The START statement may be used to position the file at the beginning or the end for subsequent retrievals'; and 9.1.13.5 3d (cite.py --check OK) reserves '23' for 'a START statement is attempted on a sequential file that has no records or that does not support the ability to position at the specified record'. NO IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS. I searched the tree myself rather than trusting the dossier: SequentialConnector.cs has no Start / StartFirstLast member of any kind (the only 'Start' identifiers are _lastReadBlockStart / _lastLineStart); FileRegistry.StartFirstLast's switch has arms only for RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector and throws MisroutedVerb for anything else; and KeyedIoBinder.BindStart short-circuits on `if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported("START on sequential-organization file ... (ISO 14.9.41 SR2 FIRST/LAST positioning - a later slice)")` — FileModel.IsSequential covering both SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL. OBSERVED (probe/seq-start/STPRB2.cob): the program COMPILES WITH NO DIAGNOSTIC and aborts at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException on the first START. Expected from GR20: records exist, so the FIRST form sets the file position indicator to 1, status '00', and the next sequential READ makes record 1 ('AAA-1') available. See finding M1 (and M2 for the edition-gate hole this same early return opens). EDITIONS: no Annex E entry, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; it depends on the FIRST/LAST phrases, which are absent from the COBOL-85 START format (the 2023 text alone cannot date them — this is the one edition claim here not derived purely from the transcription).

LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB352). Implemented whole. BindStart no longer bails on file.IsSequential; FileRegistry.StartFirstLast has its third arm; SequentialConnector.StartFirstLast walks the file with NextFrame - the ONE physical framing walk, extracted out of Read so START cannot carry a second copy of the line / varying / fixed framing rules - and repositions through SeekToRecord. MEASURED against the rule's own words in conformance:cases/9.1.13.5-Invalid-key-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb352_start_sequential_first_last: records exist, so FIRST sets the indicator to 1 with status 00 (SF=00) and the next sequential READ makes record 1 available (R2=AAA-1, per 14.9.30.4 GR21 sequential arm b); with no records the status is 23 and the invalid key condition exists (EF-INV, EF=23). The line-sequential twin is walked too (LF-OK, LSF=00, LR2=L-1). The second arm - a physical file that cannot position - is the `_reader is not { BaseStream.CanSeek: true }` test, which answers 23 rather than aborting, exactly the shape the rule states.

PB353 (2026-09-06) - THE EDITION-GATE HALF OF THE SAME RULE. PB352 landed the behaviour and, in doing so, moved the FIRST/LAST arm above the sequential bail-out, which incidentally closed this note's own repro: `START SQF FIRST` at --std 85 now reports COBOL0900 (measured on the current tree, both the sequential and the relative program). The GENERAL shape it named was still live, and on this very statement: the gate keyed on BoundKeyedStart.Mode, so EVERY OTHER path that returns before the node is built still dropped it. Measured at --std 85 before the fix - `START NOSUCHF FIRST` -> COBOL1639 alone; `START SDF FIRST` on an SD -> COBOL1692 alone. FIRST and LAST are one construct (14.9.41.2 prints one general format) and 14.9.41.3 SR2 makes the phrase mandatory on a sequential file rather than different there, so the introduction cannot depend on anything the binder resolves: the gate now fires on RECOGNITION in the VersionConformancePass parse arm (VisitStartStatement), and KeyedIoBinder holds no edition gate of any kind. The four sibling gates on the same shape moved with it (START WITH LENGTH, READ PREVIOUS, READ ADVANCING ON LOCK, INVOKE). EditionGateArmDriftTests keeps the assignment true: it derives both arms from the pass source and requires every bound-arm construct to name the resolved fact that keeps it there, and it recompiles every gated construct's own constructs.json program with the procedure-division operands broken, requiring the edition diagnostic to outlive the bind. The rule's own behaviour is unchanged - GR20/GR21 still hold through conformance:cases/9.1.13.5-Invalid-key-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb352_start_sequential_first_last.
